messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-west-2 gpu-pool 'hotpath' at 100% capacity, queue depth 12,400, 429 spike from tiered rate limiter. Autoscaler errors: heartbeat skipped x3, scale limit reached.

Sam K: Ack. I'm oncall. Triage: are these new traffic patterns? any deploys?

Priya R: No deploys in last 30m. Metrics: requests/sec doubled after 17:40 UTC. Autoscaler log shows `missed heartbeat: 3/3` then `scale blocked: pool_limit_reached`. pool_size=40, max_pool=40. Queue growth from 2k -> 12k in 7m.

Jin W: Copy. Tokenbucket stats look weird — refill_rate per-tier is higher for 'hotpath' but policy_engine is mapping many requests to 'v2-lowlat' tier incorrectly (route key mismatch). That causes rapid consumption then enforcement 429s. Snippet:
```
TOKEN_BUCKETS: {
  "v2-lowlat": {"capacity":500, "refill_per_sec":100},
  "v1-default": {"capacity":2000, "refill_per_sec":300}
}
POLICY: route_rules["/v2/*"] -> v1-default  <-- bug
```

Maya L: Opening bridge and paging CSMs. Noting customers X,Y,Z impacted — they started seeing 429s ~17:46 UTC. SLA blips likely.

Sam K: Immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily increase pool max (if capacity available) 2) Flip routing policy to force v2->v2-lowlat 3) Relax tokenbucket enforcement to allow burst while autoscaler catches up. Which are safe to do now?

Jin W: I can patch routing rule now (hotfix): `kubectl apply -f /ops/routing/v2-fix.yaml` and update tokenbucket refill to +50% for 10m. But autoscaler is blocked by pool_limit; we need to request capacity bump or enable burst_pool.

Priya R: Request to infra for +8 GPUs in us-west-2 hotpath pool. If infra can't instantly allocate, enable burst fallback to 'cpu-fallback' group (lower perf but avoids 429s). I'll open infra ticket and ping @infra-bot.

infra-bot: infra request 227149 created: increase hotpath_pool us-west-2 by 8 GPUs. ETA ~9m.

Sam K: I'll flip routing rule and increase token refill. Jin, you make the config changes. Priya, coordinate infra. Maya, notify affected accounts and status page.

Jin W: Applying patch now.
```
kubectl apply -f /ops/routing/v2-fix.yaml
kubectl edit cm tokenbucket-config --patch '{"data":{"v2-lowlat.refill":"150"}}'
```

Jin W: Patched. Routing now directs /v2/* -> v2-lowlat. Tokenbucket refill increased to 150 for v2-lowlat for 10m window.

Sam K: :thumbsup: Good. Priya, update if infra approved.

Priya R: Infra request approved, starting capacity provisioning. ETA 6m. Meanwhile enabled cpu-fallback pool for overflow.

deploy-bot: Notice: autoscaler heartbeat recovered at 17:51:02 UTC, new pool_size=48 (pending). Backpressure easing.

Maya L: Status update to customers sent. On status page: 'Degraded performance, 429s affecting some customers, mitigation in progress'.

Sam K: Observability check: error rate 429s dropped from 18% -> 3% after routing fix, queue depth falling to 4.2k. Continue to monitor for config regressions. Follow-ups: postmortem, audit tokenbucket->route mapping, add e2e test for route-to-tier correctness.

Priya R: I'm taking over oncall for next 25m to watch. Sam stepping off. Actions logged in incident tracker: INC-2026-3923. :white_check_mark:

Sam K: Thanks team. Leaving notes for postmortem: root cause = routing policy rollback + tokenbucket-tier mismatch + autoscaler pool limit. Immediate roots: misapplied canary that altered route_rules. Long-term mitigations: enforce route-to-tier tests in CI, add autoscaler soft-limits and faster burst pool activation, safer tokenbucket defaults.

Maya L: Closing bridge in 18m if metrics stable. Will draft customer postmortem and link to incident doc.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved: severity=sev2, duration=00:18:53. Tags: autoscale, tokenbucket, routing, gpu-saturation.
